name: Stratex-GF
description: A graphene-reinforced structural foam composite developed by Tessera Materials by infiltrating a closed-cell polymer foam precursor with graphene nanoplatelet suspensions before cure, creating a lightweight cellular matrix where every cell wall is graphene-reinforced. Stratex-GF achieves structural panel performance with a density near that of rigid foam insulation, enabling construction and vehicle applications where mass budget is critical. Its closed-cell architecture also provides inherent thermal and acoustic insulation properties alongside structural function.
applications: lightweight structural infill panels for hab module construction
vehicle body and interior structural cores
portable shelter and emergency habitat panels
acoustic baffling in transit and industrial facilities
story_hooks: Stratex-GF has become the material of choice for illegal Shelf-level hab expansions — it's cheap, strong enough, and easy to cut with improvised tools, meaning entire unauthorized districts are being built from it without any structural inspection.

A batch of Stratex-GF panels from a Tier 1 construction supply depot is found to contain voids in the graphene infiltration — the panels test structurally sound but the graphene content is below spec, and someone signed off on the quality certificates anyway.
A Tessera Materials quality auditor goes missing three days after filing an internal report about Stratex-GF production irregularities at a Shelf-adjacent manufacturing facility.
